subject: DPA: signature sequencing and retention carveout for Greenfield Lending
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@greenfieldlending.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenfield Legal <legal@greenfieldlending.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines + retention carveout request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Finance asked me to move forward but our legal team has a few DPA redlines attached. The two material asks are:

- A 2-year maximum retention carveout for specific financial transaction records (our regulators require 24 months for lending records).
- Explicit SCC reference for EU-origin data (we are sending a small subset of historical loan data to seed model fine-tuning in the US).

We attached Greenfield_DPA_redlines_v1.docx. Can Redwood accept the retention exception limited to the specified subdataset and the SCC language? If not, please propose alternate language and confirm who at Redwood will execute (e-sign or counter-sign). We have a compressed timeline — hoping to finalize by the end of next week.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of Integrations | Greenfield Lending
Attachment: Greenfield_DPA_redlines_v1.docx (docx, 45KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@greenfieldlending.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 11:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + retention carveout request

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the redlines. I looped in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (sales ops) so we can assess from both legal and operational angles.

Quick clarifying Qs before legal opens a formal redline:
1) Can you point to which exact tables/fields are in scope for the 24-month carveout? (a simple list or CSV would help us lock the guardrails).
2) For the SCCs, are you asking us to add the SCC clause to the DPA or to sign your version of the SCCs as a separate exhibit?

We can turn this around quickly once we have the scope. If legal accepts the carveout limited to a named dataset and we route via DocuSign, I expect execution within 2 business days after approvals.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + retention carveout request

Kim / Marissa — adding a couple of operational constraints that matter for feasibility and SLOs:

- If we accept a retention carveout for a named subdataset, we need to ensure it never flows into shared caches or persistent KV layers beyond the 24 months. That requires a data tagging + TTL enforcement on ingestion. Our infra team can enforce per-dataset TTLs but needs the table names and owner contact.
- For SCCs: Redwood's standard approach is to include SCC language in the DPA as an exhibit. Signing a separate counterparty SCC doc is doable but adds procurement steps for both sides.

Suggested path: Marissa produces a redline that includes (a) a scoped retention carveout limited to explicit object names and (b) SCC exhibit inserted into the DPA. We then route the final DPA through DocuSign to Marcus for exec signature (Marcus handles dedicated contracts for Lending vertical).

We should also let the customer know about the tagging requirement and that our infra will need engineering support on their side to populate the dataset identifier at upload time.

- Karthik
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@greenfieldlending.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 15:30:05 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA redlines + retention carveout request

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending your redlines. I've reviewed Greenfield_DPA_redlines_v1.docx and drafted a response. Key points in our response (attached):

- Retention carveout: We can accept a 24-month retention period but only if the scope is tightly defined to the dataset identifiers (table names listed). I flagged an addition requiring an agreed dataset manifest and a quarterly attestation from Greenfield confirming scope.
- SCCs: We'll include the standard EU SCC exhibit in the DPA and note that cross-border processing for the named dataset will be limited to the Redwood US region.
- Audit / Evidence: We proposed replacing a broad auditor access clause with a scoped evidence request process (SOC 2 + targeted logs) to maintain security posture while addressing your regulatory needs.

Attached: RI_response_redlines_20280726.docx (contains tracked changes and a signer map). If this looks good to Greenfield we recommend:
1) Greenfield confirms dataset identifiers (please return CSV list).
2) We update the exhibit and produce a final DPA for signature.
3) We route the final via DocuSign to Marcus Lin (exec signer), Neha to countersign on procurement ticket closure.

I marked two optional language points where legal would prefer standard Redwood language; if customer insists we can escalate to execs but that will add time.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: RI_response_redlines_20280726.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@greenfieldlending.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: signature sequencing and retention carveout for Greenfield Lending

Sarah — attaching our redline and proposed signer flow. We can move ahead on the plan below once you confirm the dataset manifest (CSV). Proposed timeline:

- Today: Greenfield returns CSV with dataset identifiers.
- Day 1 after receipt: Legal finalizes DPA and SCC exhibit.
- Day 2: DocuSign envelope sent to Marcus Lin (Redwood exec) and then to Greenfield exec for signature.

DocuSign link (preview): https://na1.docusign.net/Signing/Envelope12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

I've also attached a quick docusign-instruction.txt with guidance for their signatory (order of signing and required fields). If you can confirm the CSV and that Greenfield agrees to per-dataset TTL enforcement, we'll kick the envelope off this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
